identity.name: Prussian Confederation
alt_names: Prussian estates against the Teutonic Order

land.text: western Prussia: Gdańsk Pomerania, Chełmno Land, the region of Elbing and Marienburg

predecessors.note: 'In February 1454, the Prussian Confederation rose against the Teutonic Order's rule.' Founded earlier as a league of towns and nobles: 'On 14 March 1440' at Marienwerder (Kwidzyn).

land.text: the regions that 'formed the new Polish province of Royal Prussia'

successors.note: Second Peace of Thorn, 19 October 1466: the Confederation 'ceased to exist as such'. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1449; its House of Jagiellon row (1450-1571) is the Polish crown here. house-of-jagiellon records the land as a 1466-10 gain from teutonic-order; this dossier's vassal_end 1466-10 hands the Confederation's client land to the crown.

correction.text: western Prussia (Royal Prussia): Gdańsk Pomerania, Chełmno Land, Elbing, Marienburg, Warmia from 1466

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the rebel state's land, western Prussia: the Second Peace of Thorn has the Order renounce Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and Chełmno Land and recognises Elbing, Marienburg and Warmia as Polish, which 'formed the new Polish province of Royal Prussia'. The page names Thorn, Elbing, Danzig and Königsberg as leading cities and Kulm among the founding cities; the extent year by year is not given. The Thirteen Years' War page: the Poles took Marienburg town on 5 July 1460 and 'Teutonic forces then regained western Prussian towns', Mewe held out to 1 January 1464 and Konitz to 28 September 1466, so the held ground changed; the shape is the territory claimed, with the front a contest zone in the Teutonic Order's ledger. From March 1454 the land is a client of the Polish crown (ledger vassal_start 1454-3 to vassal_end 1466-10, counterpart house-of-jagiellon) and the Order's front is the contest zone.

ledger.note: February 1454: the Prussian Confederation rises against the Teutonic Order. 'In February 1454, the Prussian Confederation rose against the Teutonic Order's rule'; Thorn, Elbing, Danzig and Königsberg led it. The Thirteen Years' War page: the act of disobedience of 4 February 1454, then 'Two days later the confederacy started its rebellion'. The land is the researcher's reading (the page names cities, not a map).

February-March 1454: the Confederation and the Order fight for western Prussia. Delegates pledged allegiance to Casimir IV on 6 March 1454; the Confederation signed an act of incorporation in Kraków in March 1454 (Confederation page, no day given).

region.text: western Prussia, incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland by Casimir IV's act of March 1454

ledger.note: March 1454: the Confederation puts itself under the Polish crown. Casimir IV 'signed an act of incorporation in Kraków in March 1454' and the delegates 'pledged allegiance to the Polish King during the incorporation in Kraków' (Prussian Confederation page; the Thirteen Years' War page: 'pledged allegiance to Casimir on 6 March 1454'). The pages say incorporation, not vassalage: it is recorded as a client status because the Confederation went on as a body until 1466 ('ceased to exist as such') and held the land against the Order meanwhile; the land is the researcher's reading. house-of-jagiellon's ledger has a 1454-3 contest with teutonic-order over the same land. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

19 October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn ends the war. It was 'signed in the Hanseatic city of Thorn (Toruń) on 19 October 1466'; the Order 'renounced any claims to the territories of Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and Chełmno Land'.

region.text: western Prussia, now the Polish province of Royal Prussia

ledger.note: 19 October 1466: the client status ends when the land becomes the Polish province of Royal Prussia. 'Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and Chełmno Land' were 'reintegrated with Poland' and the region of Elbing and Marienburg and the Bishopric of Warmia 'also recognized as part of Poland' (Second Peace of Thorn page); the Prussian Confederation page: 'The Prussian Confederation, with its members now practically divided, ceased to exist as such.' house-of-jagiellon records the land as a 1466-10 gain from teutonic-order. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

October 1466: the Confederation ends; its lands become Royal Prussia. The regions 'formed the new Polish province of Royal Prussia' and the Confederation 'ceased to exist as such' after the 1466 settlement; Elbing, Marienburg and Warmia 'were recognized as part of Poland'.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: Second Peace of Thorn, 19 October 1466: the Order renounced Gdańsk Pomerania and Chełmno Land, Elbing, Marienburg and Warmia were recognised as part of Poland, and the Confederation's land formed Royal Prussia.
wars.note: Marienburg, Dirschau and Eylau castles passed to the Polish army on 6 June 1457; the Poles took Marienburg town on 5 July 1460; Mewe capitulated 1 January 1464; Konitz fell 28 September 1466. The war page's text gives 10 October 1466 for the peace and its infobox 19 October.

certainty.note: A moving front; no page opened gives the Confederation's frontier in any one year, and the Thirteen Years' War page records cities changing hands.

sources.title: Prussian Confederation
sources.note: 1440 founding, February 1454 rising, March 1454 incorporation act, 1466 end; no seat, no area.

sources.title: Thirteen Years' War (1454-1466)
sources.note: Used for the 4 February and 6 March 1454 dates and the campaign chronology.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks (new slug prussian-confederation; a league of Prussian towns and nobles founded at Marienwerder on 14 March 1440, in revolt from February 1454). It is the counterpart of the contest events in the teutonic-order ledger. Held land is the 'West Prussia' region, an approximation of the Order's lost half; the pages give no year-by-year map. The act of incorporation into the Kingdom of Poland (March 1454) makes the territory a Polish protectorate or part of the crown: the house-of-jagiellon dossier should carry a vassal_start/vassal_end (or the land itself, as Royal Prussia from 1466) with counterpart prussian-confederation; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1449 and the House of Jagiellon row starts in 1450. Royal Prussia (1466-1569/1772) has no Cliopatria row and may need a dossier of its own. No capital or seat is named on the pages opened, so capitals is empty; the Confederation was 'led' by Thorn, Elbing, Danzig and Königsberg, with Johannes von Baysen as its leader. The Wikidata id is unknown (the site cannot reach wikidata.org). Pages: 3 opened (a rebel state added, outside any budget). REVIEW REPAIRS 2026-10-25 (author). The review found no link to the Polish crown although the Confederation's lands were incorporated in March 1454. Chosen of the two options: vassal_start 1454-3 and vassal_end 1466-10 with counterpart house-of-jagiellon (the dossier keeps its twelve years and its colour, as rule 5 asks for rebel-held land, shown as a client of Poland), not an end in March 1454 with a merge: the Prussian Confederation page says it 'ceased to exist as such' only after 1466 and the Order's contest events here keep counterpart prussian-confederation. The pages (Prussian Confederation: 'act of incorporation in Kraków in March 1454', delegates 'pledged allegiance'; Thirteen Years' War: 6 March 1454) call it incorporation, not vassalage, so the status is a reading (confidence 2). Consequence for others: house-of-jagiellon (eu-15) has a 1454-3 contest and a 1466-10 gain with teutonic-order but no relation to prussian-confederation; it should carry vassal_start 1454-3 / vassal_end 1466-10 with counterpart prussian-confederation to mirror this dossier. Royal Prussia (1466-1569/1772) still has no row; the Order's eastern part stayed a fief (teutonic-order ledger 1466-10).
